2. The Family Court decreed the suit holding that the defendant-petitioner (husband) and the plaintiff-opposite party (wife) are lawfully wedded couple and directed the defendant to pay a sum of Taka 5,000.00 to the plaintiff as against prompt dower and to bring her back to his own house and discharge his marital obligation, alternatively to pay her Taka 500.00 per month for her maintenance. 

 22. Where either the husband or wife has without lawful ground withdrawn from the society of the other or neglected to perform the obligations imposed by law or by the contract of marriage the Court may decree restitution of conjugal rights and may put either party on terms securing to the other the enjoyment of his or her legal rights (Ref Tyabji's Muslim Law 4th Edn paragraph 87; Abdur Rahim, Md. Jurs, 334; Anis Begum vs Md Mostafa Wale (1933) 55 All 743). The said right however is not absolute. The Koran enjoins husbands to keep their wives with kindness. 

 24. However it is nether desirable nor expected that the Court should pass adecree of restitution of conjugal rights where the relationship of adjustment between the husband and wife is lost or it is otherwise inequitable impractical or impossible to implement. In the present case it has been rightly ordered that if the husband fails to live together in the discharge of his marital obligations he is to pay a sum of Taka 500.00 per month for her maintenance. 

 26. In view of the discussions made above. I do not find that the impugned judgment and decree suffer from any illegality or error of law.
